text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert fired - decode-pool-3 GPUs reporting OOMs and container restarts. error rate spiked for streaming endpoints. Auto-pages sent to oncall.

Tori: I got paged. spinning up context - what's the customer impact?

alex: Looks like a run of runaway generations hitting max_tokens >> normal. Several streams show continuous decode with no stop token, filling GPU memory until OOM.

maya: We see "CUDA out of memory" from decode process on pod decode-rt-3b-7. Logs show multiple requests with content-length spikes, likely bad client config.

lee: Confirmed pod restarted twice in 6m. kube events: CrashLoopBackOff then oom-kill.

ops-oncall: I'm putting a temporary routing rule to drain decode-pool-3 and route new streaming requests to decode-pool-1 (lower-latency but smaller batch capacity). Doing a rolling label update now.

Tori: Good. Can someone list quick mitigations we can do live to reduce customer error rate?

alex: Short list: 1) Patch routing to avoid the affected GPU pool (ops doing). 2) Apply per-connection token cap at the gateway to stop runaway sessions. 3) Hot-restart affected pods with GDB/strace logs off to avoid further OOM churn. 4) Temporarily disable streaming for the largest model variant for this pool.

maya: Started a rate-limit rule on the request proxy: `rlimit per_conn 5000 tokens` (temp).

lee: I pushed a quick canary config to the shard manager to deny `max_tokens > 20000` for streaming routes hitting decode-pool-3.

Tori: Nice. Any sign of a misconfigured client param that correlates?

alex: Customer-side logs (from their support bundle) show a bot that sets `max_tokens: 100000` and uses `stream: true` w/o stop tokens. So it's a bad client. We've informed support.

incident-bot: Pager duty: `#oncall-sre` acknowledged by @tori.

ops-oncall: Routing change completed: decode-pool-3 marked draining; new sessions go to decode-pool-1 and decode-pool-2. Old sessions kept for 5m to avoid mid-stream truncation.

Tori: I'm going to escalate to eng-runtime for a potential kernel-level mem leak or a decoder path that doesn't release KV cache on early termination. @eng-runtime can you join?

eng-runtime: On it. Initial hypothesis: when `stream=true` and no eos token produced, KV cache grows unbounded for some early model variants; combined with long token window causes OOM. We have a patch to force-stop after X tokens on the server side as a safety net.

maya: Captured stack traces and last 200 lines of logs from pod. Pasting snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T08:12:34Z] ERROR decode: cuda runtime error(2): out of memory at /runtime/decode.cu:1124
[2026-03-15T08:12:34Z] WARN session: token_count=98712, stream=true, client_id=acct-74
[2026-03-15T08:12:36Z] INFO kube: pod decode-rt-3b-7 terminated with oom_kill
```

lee: Per-customer impact: one enterprise customer saw ~22% of streams dropped for a 9-minute window while pool drained. Non-critical batch endpoints unaffected.

alex: Metrics: token-per-second across decode pools jumped 6x at incident start. GPU mem utilization hit 99% on affected nodes.

Tori: Action items: - ops: keep pool drained until patch & restart complete - eng-runtime: deploy server-side token safety net (force-stop at 40k tokens for stream sessions) - support: notify affected customer with timeline and mitigation steps - infra: capture full pod images & attach to incident artifacts.

ops-oncall: Draining extended, currently 14 pods drained, 3 still restarting slowly. Updated autoscaler to avoid scaling into drained subnet.

eng-runtime: Pushing hotfix: server enforces `stream_token_hard_limit=40000` for all streaming requests as emergency guard. Deploying to hosted control plane now.

maya: After patch rollout, observed immediate drop in new OOMs. Error-rate for streaming endpoints reduced to baseline within 3m.

Tori: Re-enable streaming to trimmed model variants only?

eng-runtime: Re-enabled streaming on pool-1/2 with a small model fallback for any requests that exceed token softness. Also added a server-side stop-check to free KV cache when inference stalls > 30s.

alex: Customer facing message drafted: "We observed a GPU OOM issue triggered by unusually large streaming requests from a client process. We applied routing and server-side safeguards which mitigated OOMs; affected streams were dropped while we drained the pool. We're pushing a permanent fix and recommending customers enforce client-side max_tokens."

ops-oncall: Rolling restarts complete on decode-pool-3 nodes. No new OOMs observed post-restart + patch.

Tori: Assigning follow-ups: `eng-runtime` to submit PR for permanent guard + unit tests; `infra` to add a streaming session sentinel metric; `support` to send post-incident note to customer.

lee: Logging note: add structured cause tags for OOMs: `oom.cause=runaway_generation` `oom.client_max_tokens` for better triage.

incident-bot: Incident page created: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1959876543 (severity: P2, duration: ~25m).

Tori: Thanks all. Closing the immediate paging loop. We'll keep the incident open for postmortem and RCA. :thumbsup:

maya: Adding final timestamps to the incident doc and uploading the pod core dumps to the artifacts bucket.

alex: I'll follow up with a short playbook update for streaming-safety best practices.

eng-runtime: Filed PR: enforce token hard limit, add KV-cache GC on stall, add E2E test simulating no-stop-token condition. Link: https://git.redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/1123

Tori: Good work. Moving to postmortem channel after this thread.

ops-oncall: Note for SRE rotation: watch for regressions after deploying performance improvements; we've left a temporary dashboard for the next 48h.
